summary: Abandoned but not Forgotten is an interactive digital exhibit cataloging 16 historic NASA missions and over 191 pieces of human hardware left behind on the Moon and Mars between 1966 and 2021. Space exploration is often told through launches and landings, overlooking the boosters, heat shields, parachutes, landers, and rovers that remain scattered across two worlds. Our project transforms raw planetary coordinates and mission logs into an engaging visual timeline, interactive spacecraft anatomy diagrams, planetary maps, curated mission footage, and S.O.S., an off-world survival mini-game where players scavenge real crash and landing sites to build a transmitter. Built as an installable Progressive Web App (PWA) using NASA LRO, HiRISE, and JPL data, it makes spaceflight history tangible, educational, and accessible offline.
details:
"Abandoned but not Forgotten" is an interactive web museum and Progressive Web App (PWA) covering 16 Moon and Mars missions—from Surveyor 1 (1966) and Apollo 11–17 to Viking 1, Spirit, Opportunity, InSight, and Perseverance. Users can:

  • Explore the 5-Phase Journey: Step through Launch, Cruise, Arrival/Landing, Surface Operations, and End of Life for each mission with narrated audio playback.
  • Inspect Vehicle Anatomy & Machinery Manifests: Click individual spacecraft components (fairings, stages, descent engines, rovers, retroreflectors) to learn their exact fate.
  • View Planetary Maps: Locate verified LRO/LROC and Mars landing coordinates across lunar and Martian topographic maps.
  • Watch Mission Footage: Compare original launch broadcasts with final movement/landing footage for all 16 missions.
  • Play S.O.S. (Off-World Survival Sim): A strategy mini-game set at the 16 real landing sites where players scavenge actual mission debris (solar arrays, batteries, dishes) to wire up a transmitter before life support runs out.

Tools & Technologies Used

  • Frontend: Vanilla HTML5, CSS3, and modular JavaScript (data.js, manifest.js, vehicles.js, app.js, game.js, footage.js, narrator.js).
  • Offline & App Support: Web App Manifest (manifest.webmanifest) and Service Worker (sw.js) for full offline installability.
  • Data & Media: Georeferenced coordinates from NASA NSSDCA, LRO/LROC, and HiRISE, paired with public-domain NASA imagery and archival YouTube footage.

Impact & Creativity Instead of treating space missions as static encyclopedia entries, we reframed space exploration around the physical artifacts humanity left behind—turning orbital coordinates and engineering manifests into an interactive story and survival game.
